final-20261113-qa2--heavy-vehicle--b01-t.instructions:
TASK 3: WORKSHOP SAFETY, VEHICLE
SUPPORT AND TECHNICAL MEASUREMENT
Heavy Vehicle Service and Maintenance Technician Level 3 | Block 1 | v1.1
TIME
90 minutes (adapt to workplace
conditions)
EVIDENCE
Practical | Knowledge |
Documentation
PROGRAMME POINT
Weeks 1-10 | Months 1-3
Your task
Prepare a heavy-vehicle work area, complete a task-specific risk check, select suitable tools and safely support an
unloaded vehicle or approved training rig before taking and recording technical measurements.
What you must do
1
Confirm the job instruction, hazards, authority and emergency arrangements.
2
Select PPE, tools, support equipment and technical information.
3
Secure and support the vehicle or rig at approved points; verify stability before work.
4
Take specified measurements, apply tolerances and record results accurately.
5
Reinstate the work area, account for tools and report defects or limitations.
What good evidence looks like
SAFE CONTROL
No work beneath a raised vehicle or cab until approved secondary
support is fitted and stability is verified.
CORRECT METHOD
A logical sequence using current manufacturer, DVSA, company
and task-specific information.
ACCURATE EVIDENCE
Actual values, test conditions, units, findings and evidence
references recorded clearly.
SOUND DECISIONS
A justified serviceability, repair, referral or recovery decision
followed by appropriate verification.
You will need
•
Unloaded heavy vehicle or approved rig
•
Rated chocks, stands and lifting equipment
•
Measuring tools and manufacturer data
•
PPE, risk check and job card
SOW ALIGNMENT
Block 1 - Motor Vehicle Foundation Skills
KSB evidence focus: Controlled Foundation Skills mapping; primary heavy-vehicle link K4

final-20261113-qa2--heavy-vehicle--b01-t.instructions:
TASK 4: 24V ELECTRICAL MEASUREMENT AND
TECHNICAL DOCUMENTATION
Heavy Vehicle Service and Maintenance Technician Level 3 | Block 1 | v1.1
TIME
90 minutes (adapt to workplace
conditions)
EVIDENCE
Practical | Knowledge |
Documentation
PROGRAMME POINT
Weeks 1-10 | Months 1-3
Your task
Use technical information and a digital multimeter to check a protected 24 V training circuit or heavy-vehicle
low-voltage system, then complete a clear technical record and handover.
What you must do
1
Identify circuit hazards, voltage level, isolation needs and safe test points.
2
Select and prove the meter, leads and range before connection.
3
Measure supply voltage, voltage drop and resistance only where the procedure permits.
4
Interpret results against the circuit diagram and specification.
5
Record findings, reinstate protection and communicate the result.
What good evidence looks like
SAFE CONTROL
Follow manufacturer isolation procedures; never bridge circuit
protection or probe connectors in a way that causes damage.
CORRECT METHOD
A logical sequence using current manufacturer, DVSA, company
and task-specific information.
ACCURATE EVIDENCE
Actual values, test conditions, units, findings and evidence
references recorded clearly.
SOUND DECISIONS
A justified serviceability, repair, referral or recovery decision
followed by appropriate verification.
You will need
•
24 V training board or heavy vehicle
•
Digital multimeter and fused leads
•
Wiring diagram and specifications
•
PPE and job-card documentation
SOW ALIGNMENT
Block 1 - Motor Vehicle Foundation Skills
KSB evidence focus: Controlled Foundation Skills mapping; primary heavy-vehicle link K4

TASK 3: FULL HEAVY VEHICLE AND TRAILER
SAFETY INSPECTION
Heavy Vehicle Service and Maintenance Technician Level 3 | Block 2 | v1.1
TIME
90 minutes (adapt to workplace
conditions)
EVIDENCE
Practical | Knowledge |
Documentation
PROGRAMME POINT
Weeks 11-26 | Months 3-7
Your task
Complete a systematic safety inspection of a heavy vehicle and, where available, its trailer. Use current DVSA and
manufacturer information, classify defects and produce an auditable inspection record.
What you must do
1
Confirm vehicle/trailer identity, inspection scope and maintenance history.
2
Secure the combination and follow the approved inspection sequence.
3
Inspect safety-critical systems and record actual condition and measurements.
4
Classify defects, stop unsafe work and escalate immediate risks.
5
Complete the inspection record and final quality check.
What good evidence looks like
SAFE CONTROL
Apply parking, chocking, isolation and support procedures; do not
enter crush zones or release stored energy without control.
CORRECT METHOD
A logical sequence using current manufacturer, DVSA, company
and task-specific information.
ACCURATE EVIDENCE
Actual values, test conditions, units, findings and evidence
references recorded clearly.
SOUND DECISIONS
A justified serviceability, repair, referral or recovery decision
followed by appropriate verification.
You will need
•
Heavy vehicle and trailer
•
DVSA inspection manual and manufacturer data
•
Inspection, lighting and measuring equipment
•
PPE, defect report and maintenance record
SOW ALIGNMENT
Block 2 - Inspection, Planned Maintenance and Operator's Licence Compliance
KSB evidence focus: K5, K6, S5; reinforced S7, S8, S10, S11, B1-B3

conditions)

Practical | Knowledge |
Documentation

Your task

record so that it supports the operator's planned-maintenance and legal obligations.

1
Review the service schedule, history, recalls and job authorisation.
2

3

5

Prevent unintended engine start and vehicle movement; control
hot components, fluids and environmental releases.
CORRECT METHOD
A logical sequence using current manufacturer, DVSA, company
and task-specific information.
ACCURATE EVIDENCE
Actual values, test conditions, units, findings and evidence
references recorded clearly.
SOUND DECISIONS
A justified serviceability, repair, referral or recovery decision
followed by appropriate verification.
You will need
•
Heavy vehicle and service schedule
•
Approved fluids, filters and consumables
•
Torque tools and service equipment
•
Waste controls and maintenance documentation

Heavy Vehicle Service and Maintenance Technician Level 3 | Block 3 | v1.1
TIME
90 minutes (adapt to workplace
conditions)
EVIDENCE
Practical | Knowledge |
Documentation
PROGRAMME POINT
Weeks 27-42 | Months 7-11
Your task
Inspect steering, mechanical/air suspension, axle and hub components on a heavy vehicle. Measure selected wear or
end float, diagnose the likely cause of abnormal tyre wear and recommend action.
What you must do
1
Confirm reported symptoms, vehicle configuration and inspection limits.
2
Secure and support the vehicle; depressurise or restrain suspension where required.
3
Inspect steering linkages, suspension, axle, hubs and mountings.
4
Measure selected clearances, end float or geometry and compare with data.
5
Record defects, root-cause reasoning and repair/verification recommendations.
What good evidence looks like
SAFE CONTROL
Use approved chassis stands and suspension controls; never rely
on air pressure, a jack or self-levelling suspension for support.
CORRECT METHOD
A logical sequence using current manufacturer, DVSA, company
and task-specific information.
ACCURATE EVIDENCE
Actual values, test conditions, units, findings and evidence
references recorded clearly.
SOUND DECISIONS
A justified serviceability, repair, referral or recovery decision
followed by appropriate verification.
You will need
•
Heavy vehicle or chassis rig
•
Rated lifting/support equipment
•
Dial gauge, alignment and wear-check tools
•
Manufacturer/DVSA data and PPE
SOW ALIGNMENT

TASK 3: AIR PRESSURE BUILD-UP, LEAK AND
WARNING-DEVICE TESTS
Heavy Vehicle Service and Maintenance Technician Level 3 | Block 4 | v1.1
TIME
90 minutes (adapt to workplace
conditions)
EVIDENCE
Practical | Knowledge |
Documentation
PROGRAMME POINT
Weeks 43-58 | Months 12-15
Your task
Test air-brake system pressure build-up, governor operation, warning devices and leakage on a heavy vehicle. Compare
results with approved data and report any safety-critical defect.
What you must do
1
Review the pneumatic diagram, test method and vehicle-specific precautions.
2
Secure the vehicle and connect calibrated pressure/test equipment safely.
3
Record pressure build-up, cut-in/cut-out and low-pressure warning operation.
4
Carry out specified static/applied leakage tests without entering danger zones.
5
Interpret results, restore the system and complete a safety-critical report.
What good evidence looks like
SAFE CONTROL
Chock the vehicle and keep clear of actuators, suspension and
moving linkages; stored air must be exhausted by the approved
method before disassembly.
CORRECT METHOD
A logical sequence using current manufacturer, DVSA, company
and task-specific information.
ACCURATE EVIDENCE
Actual values, test conditions, units, findings and evidence
references recorded clearly.
SOUND DECISIONS
A justified serviceability, repair, referral or recovery decision
followed by appropriate verification.
You will need
•
Heavy vehicle with air brakes
•
Calibrated pressure gauges and timer
•
Pneumatic diagram and test specifications
•
Chocks, PPE and defect record
SOW ALIGNMENT
Block 4 - Air Braking, Pneumatic and Hydraulic Systems
KSB evidence focus: K1, S1, S3; reinforced K3-K6, K10, S4-S10, B2-B3
Task reference: HV_L3_Block_4_Task_3_Air_Pressure_Build_Up_Leak_and_Warning_Device_Tests

final-20261113-qa2--heavy-vehicle--b04-t.instructions:
TASK 4: FOUNDATION BRAKE INSPECTION AND
EBS DIAGNOSTIC CHECK
Heavy Vehicle Service and Maintenance Technician Level 3 | Block 4 | v1.1
TIME
90 minutes (adapt to workplace
conditions)
EVIDENCE
Practical | Knowledge |
Documentation
PROGRAMME POINT
Weeks 43-58 | Months 12-15
Your task
Inspect selected foundation-brake components and use EBS information to investigate a reported brake warning or
imbalance. Produce a repair plan and verification requirements.
What you must do
1
Confirm symptoms, warning status, technical data and safe test boundaries.
2
Secure/support the vehicle and isolate or restrain spring-brake energy as specified.
3
Inspect disc/drum, friction, actuator and mechanical components; record wear.
4
Read EBS faults/data and test relevant sensors, wiring or pneumatic controls.
5
Identify root cause, record repair authorisation needs and define final tests.
What good evidence looks like
SAFE CONTROL
Do not dismantle a spring-brake chamber; use approved
restraint/isolation methods and follow the manufacturer
procedure for brake work.
CORRECT METHOD
A logical sequence using current manufacturer, DVSA, company
and task-specific information.
ACCURATE EVIDENCE
Actual values, test conditions, units, findings and evidence
references recorded clearly.
SOUND DECISIONS
A justified serviceability, repair, referral or recovery decision
followed by appropriate verification.
You will need
•
Heavy vehicle or brake/EBS rig
•
Brake wear and pressure measuring tools
•
Approved scan tool and electrical test equipment
•
Manufacturer/DVSA data, PPE and restraints
SOW ALIGNMENT
Block 4 - Air Braking, Pneumatic and Hydraulic Systems
KSB evidence focus: K1, S1, S3; reinforced K3-K6, K10, S4-S10, B2-B3
Task reference: HV_L3_Block_4_Task_4_Foundation_Brake_Inspection_and_EBS_Diagnostic_Check

final-20261113-qa2--heavy-vehicle--b05-t.instructions:
TASK 3: 24V STARTING AND CHARGING
SYSTEM DIAGNOSIS
Heavy Vehicle Service and Maintenance Technician Level 3 | Block 5 | v1.1
TIME
90 minutes (adapt to workplace
conditions)
EVIDENCE
Practical | Knowledge |
Documentation
PROGRAMME POINT
Weeks 59-74 | Months 16-20
Your task
Investigate a heavy vehicle with slow cranking or poor battery charging. Test the 24 V battery set, starting circuit and
alternator control, then identify the underlying fault and verify the result.
What you must do
1
Confirm symptoms, battery configuration, system voltage and technical data.
2
Inspect, isolate as required, and test both batteries under controlled conditions.
3
Measure cranking voltage/current and positive/ground voltage drop.
4
Test charging output, control and voltage at specified conditions.
5
Diagnose root cause, record repair action and complete post-repair verification.
What good evidence looks like
SAFE CONTROL
Control ignition/start authorisation, battery gases and high fault
current; use insulated terminal protection and the specified
disconnect sequence.
CORRECT METHOD
A logical sequence using current manufacturer, DVSA, company
and task-specific information.
ACCURATE EVIDENCE
Actual values, test conditions, units, findings and evidence
references recorded clearly.
SOUND DECISIONS
A justified serviceability, repair, referral or recovery decision
followed by appropriate verification.
You will need
•
Heavy vehicle or 24 V starting/charging rig
•
Battery tester, multimeter and current clamp
•
Wiring diagram and specifications
•
PPE, terminal protection and job card
SOW ALIGNMENT
Block 5 - 12/24V Electrical, Electronic and Networked Systems
KSB evidence focus: K3, S6, S9; reinforced K1, K4, K10, S1-S4, S8, S10-S11, B2-B3
Task reference: HV_L3_Block_5_Task_3_24V_Starting_and_Charging_System_Diagnosis

final-20261113-qa2--heavy-vehicle--b05-t.instructions:
TASK 4: CAN NETWORK AND TRAILER
ELECTRICAL FAULT DIAGNOSIS
Heavy Vehicle Service and Maintenance Technician Level 3 | Block 5 | v1.1
TIME
90 minutes (adapt to workplace
conditions)
EVIDENCE
Practical | Knowledge |
Documentation
PROGRAMME POINT
Weeks 59-74 | Months 16-20
Your task
Diagnose a network or trailer-electrical concern using circuit information, scan-tool data and targeted measurements.
Avoid unnecessary parts replacement and document the evidence trail.
What you must do
1
Confirm the symptom, affected systems and any recent work.
2
Obtain the network topology, connector information and test limits.
3
Complete visual, supply/ground and circuit-protection checks.
4
Use scan data and targeted voltage/resistance/waveform tests as authorised.
5
Identify root cause, repair/referral action and post-repair network checks.
What good evidence looks like
SAFE CONTROL
Follow network shutdown and battery-isolation requirements; do
not pierce sealed wiring or short communication circuits.
CORRECT METHOD
A logical sequence using current manufacturer, DVSA, company
and task-specific information.
ACCURATE EVIDENCE
Actual values, test conditions, units, findings and evidence
references recorded clearly.
SOUND DECISIONS
A justified serviceability, repair, referral or recovery decision
followed by appropriate verification.
You will need
•
Heavy vehicle/trailer or network rig
•
OEM-capable scan tool
•
Multimeter, breakout leads and optional oscilloscope
•
Wiring/topology data and PPE
SOW ALIGNMENT
Block 5 - 12/24V Electrical, Electronic and Networked Systems
KSB evidence focus: K3, S6, S9; reinforced K1, K4, K10, S1-S4, S8, S10-S11, B2-B3

TASK 3: ENGINE, FUEL AND COOLING SYSTEM
DIAGNOSIS
Heavy Vehicle Service and Maintenance Technician Level 3 | Block 6 | v1.1
TIME
90 minutes (adapt to workplace
conditions)
EVIDENCE
Practical | Knowledge |
Documentation
PROGRAMME POINT
Weeks 75-90 | Months 20-24
Your task
Investigate a heavy vehicle with reduced performance or an abnormal temperature/pressure concern. Use technical
data, live information and mechanical tests to locate the cause.
What you must do
1
Confirm symptoms, operating conditions, fluid levels and fault history.
2
Inspect air, fuel, lubrication and cooling systems before intrusive testing.
3
Use scan data and authorised pressure, temperature or flow tests.
4
Compare results, identify interactions and isolate the likely root cause.
5
Record repair action, environmental controls and verification requirements.
What good evidence looks like
SAFE CONTROL
Allow systems to cool and depressurise as specified; do not open
high-pressure fuel systems without the manufacturer procedure
and suitable authority.
CORRECT METHOD
A logical sequence using current manufacturer, DVSA, company
and task-specific information.
ACCURATE EVIDENCE
Actual values, test conditions, units, findings and evidence
references recorded clearly.
SOUND DECISIONS
A justified serviceability, repair, referral or recovery decision
followed by appropriate verification.
You will need
•
Heavy vehicle or engine rig
•
Scan tool and pressure/temperature equipment
•
Manufacturer test data
•
PPE, spill control and job card
SOW ALIGNMENT
Block 6 - Engines, Fuel, Emissions, Thermal Management and Emerging Technology

TASK 4: DPF/SCR AFTERTREATMENT
DIAGNOSIS AND VERIFICATION
Heavy Vehicle Service and Maintenance Technician Level 3 | Block 6 | v1.1
TIME
90 minutes (adapt to workplace
conditions)
EVIDENCE
Practical | Knowledge |
Documentation
PROGRAMME POINT
Weeks 75-90 | Months 20-24
Your task
Investigate an emissions warning or derate involving DPF/SCR/AdBlue systems. Use data and physical checks to find the
cause and decide whether regeneration, repair or referral is appropriate.
What you must do
1
Confirm warning history, operating pattern, fluid quality and relevant DTCs.
2
Inspect exhaust, dosing, sensor and wiring condition safely.
3
Record temperatures, pressures, NOx or dosing data against specifications.
4
Determine whether prerequisites permit an authorised regeneration or functional test.
5
Identify root cause, complete permitted action and verify emissions-system status.
What good evidence looks like
SAFE CONTROL
Regeneration requires an approved exclusion zone, ventilation
and continuous monitoring; hot exhaust and fire risks must
remain controlled.
CORRECT METHOD
A logical sequence using current manufacturer, DVSA, company
and task-specific information.
ACCURATE EVIDENCE
Actual values, test conditions, units, findings and evidence
references recorded clearly.
SOUND DECISIONS
A justified serviceability, repair, referral or recovery decision
followed by appropriate verification.
You will need
•
Heavy vehicle or aftertreatment rig
•
OEM-capable scan tool
•
Temperature/pressure and fluid-quality test equipment
•
Technical data, exclusion controls and PPE
SOW ALIGNMENT
Block 6 - Engines, Fuel, Emissions, Thermal Management and Emerging Technology

final-20261113-qa2--heavy-vehicle--b07-t.instructions:
Heavy Vehicle Service and Maintenance Technician Level 3 | Block 7 | v1.1
TIME
90 minutes (adapt to workplace
conditions)
EVIDENCE
Practical | Knowledge |
Documentation
PROGRAMME POINT
Weeks 91-106 | Months 24-28
Your task
Investigate a reported driveline noise or vibration on a heavy vehicle. Inspect the
clutch/transmission/propshaft/final-drive path, use safe measurements and produce a justified repair plan.
What you must do
1
Clarify symptom, load/speed conditions, history and road-test authority.
2
Secure the vehicle and inspect mounts, shafts, joints, bearings and lubricant condition.
3
Measure free play, run-out, angles or other specified values.
4
Use findings to distinguish imbalance, misalignment, wear or control concerns.
5
Plan parts, time, risks, verification and customer/operator communication.
What good evidence looks like
SAFE CONTROL
Prevent engine start and driveline rotation unless an approved
controlled test requires it; never work beneath an inadequately
supported vehicle.
CORRECT METHOD
A logical sequence using current manufacturer, DVSA, company
and task-specific information.
ACCURATE EVIDENCE
Actual values, test conditions, units, findings and evidence
references recorded clearly.
SOUND DECISIONS
A justified serviceability, repair, referral or recovery decision
followed by appropriate verification.
You will need
•
Heavy vehicle or driveline rig
•
Rated support and driveline measuring tools
•
Manufacturer specifications and lubricant data
•
PPE, job card and repair-planning information
SOW ALIGNMENT
Block 7 - Transmission, Driveline, Hydraulics, Ancillaries and Complex Repair

final-20261113-qa2--heavy-vehicle--b07-t.instructions:
TASK 4: PTO AND HYDRAULIC ANCILLARY
FAULT DIAGNOSIS
Heavy Vehicle Service and Maintenance Technician Level 3 | Block 7 | v1.1
TIME
90 minutes (adapt to workplace
conditions)
EVIDENCE
Practical | Knowledge |
Documentation
PROGRAMME POINT
Weeks 91-106 | Months 24-28
Your task
Diagnose a PTO-driven hydraulic ancillary concern, such as a tail-lift or tipping system fault. Control stored energy, test
the system and produce a safe repair and verification plan.
What you must do
1
Confirm operating complaint, equipment limits and authorised test conditions.
2
Isolate/support the ancillary and release stored pressure by the approved method.
3
Inspect PTO engagement, fluid, hoses, filters, pumps, valves and actuators.
4
Measure pressure/flow or electrical control signals at specified points.
5
Identify root cause and document repair, contamination control and proof testing.
What good evidence looks like
SAFE CONTROL
Mechanically support raised equipment and establish an exclusion
zone; never rely on hydraulic pressure to support a load.
CORRECT METHOD
A logical sequence using current manufacturer, DVSA, company
and task-specific information.
ACCURATE EVIDENCE
Actual values, test conditions, units, findings and evidence
references recorded clearly.
SOUND DECISIONS
A justified serviceability, repair, referral or recovery decision
followed by appropriate verification.
You will need
•
Heavy vehicle ancillary or hydraulic rig
•
Rated supports and exclusion controls
•
Hydraulic pressure/flow and electrical test equipment
•
Hydraulic diagram, specifications and PPE
SOW ALIGNMENT
Block 7 - Transmission, Driveline, Hydraulics, Ancillaries and Complex Repair
KSB evidence focus: K8, K10, B2; reinforced K1-K4, K6, K11, S1-S6, S8-S10, B3

TASK 3: ADVANCED INTERMITTENT FAULT
DIAGNOSTIC INVESTIGATION
Heavy Vehicle Service and Maintenance Technician Level 3 | Block 8 | v1.1
TIME
90 minutes (adapt to workplace
conditions)
EVIDENCE
Practical | Knowledge |
Documentation
PROGRAMME POINT
Weeks 107-117 | Months 28-31
Your task
Plan and carry out an evidence-led investigation of an intermittent heavy-vehicle electrical, pneumatic or mechanical
fault. Capture repeatable evidence and avoid speculative parts replacement.
What you must do
1
Confirm the symptom precisely and gather driver, history and environmental information.
2
Create a staged test plan with expected values and decision points.
3
Reproduce the concern safely and capture scan, measurement or pressure evidence.
4
Analyse correlations, challenge assumptions and isolate root cause.
5
Record the evidence trail, limitations, repair/referral and verification plan.
What good evidence looks like
SAFE CONTROL
Only reproduce faults under approved conditions; stop if testing
compromises braking, steering, vehicle control or public safety.
CORRECT METHOD
A logical sequence using current manufacturer, DVSA, company
and task-specific information.
ACCURATE EVIDENCE
Actual values, test conditions, units, findings and evidence
references recorded clearly.
SOUND DECISIONS
A justified serviceability, repair, referral or recovery decision
followed by appropriate verification.
You will need
•
Heavy vehicle or diagnostic case-study rig
•
Appropriate scan, electrical or pressure equipment
•
Technical information and known-good data
•
Data capture sheet, PPE and job card
SOW ALIGNMENT
Block 8 - Advanced Diagnostic Strategy and Roadside Assistance
KSB evidence focus: K11, S10; reinforced K3, K4, K10, S2-S4, S6, S8-S9, S11, B1-B3

TIME
90 minutes (adapt to workplace
conditions)
EVIDENCE
Practical | Knowledge |
Documentation
PROGRAMME POINT
Weeks 107-117 | Months 28-31
Your task
Respond to a simulated heavy-vehicle roadside breakdown. Assess scene risk, complete safe triage, communicate with
stakeholders and decide whether repair, restricted movement, referral or recovery is appropriate.
What you must do
1
Obtain location, vehicle, load, symptom and immediate-risk information.
2
Complete dynamic scene assessment and establish personal/vehicle protection.
3
Carry out non-intrusive triage within authority and available safe access.
4
Evaluate defect severity, operating limits and recovery/referral options.
5
Communicate the decision and complete a compliant roadside record.
What good evidence looks like
SAFE CONTROL
This is a controlled simulation unless authorised roadside
arrangements exist; personal safety and third-party traffic risk
take priority over vehicle repair.
CORRECT METHOD
A logical sequence using current manufacturer, DVSA, company
and task-specific information.
ACCURATE EVIDENCE
Actual values, test conditions, units, findings and evidence
references recorded clearly.
SOUND DECISIONS
A justified serviceability, repair, referral or recovery decision
followed by appropriate verification.
You will need
•
Roadside scenario or controlled training area
•
Visibility/scene-control equipment
•
Vehicle technical and recovery information
•
Communication device, PPE and roadside record

followed by appropriate verification.

TASK 3: INTEGRATED FULL VEHICLE AND
TRAILER INSPECTION



Heavy Vehicle Service and Maintenance Technician Level 3 | Block 10 | v1.3





  TIME                                EVIDENCE                       PROGRAMME POINT

  90 minutes (adapt to workplace           Practical | Knowledge |               Weeks 129-135 | Months 34-35
  conditions)                           Documentation


  Your task


Complete a timed, developmental full vehicle and trailer inspection that integrates safety, technical information, defect
classification, communication and record quality across the programme.


 What you must do


  1    Plan the task, confirm scope, vehicle/trailer identity and safe setup.


  2    Complete the attached checklist using current technical and DVSA information.


  3    Record measurements and defects, including safety-critical escalation.


  4    Explain priorities and required actions to the assessor/workplace mentor.


  5    Complete final QA, evidence references and an accurate maintenance record.



 What good evidence looks like




   SAFE CONTROL                                   CORRECT METHOD

     All safety-critical systems, support arrangements and                 A logical sequence using current manufacturer, DVSA, company
    stored-energy controls remain subject to the relevant                  and task-specific information.
    manufacturer and workplace procedures.



   ACCURATE EVIDENCE                            SOUND DECISIONS

    Actual values, test conditions, units, findings and evidence             A justified serviceability, repair, referral or recovery decision
    references recorded clearly.                                              followed by appropriate verification.




 You will need


 •  Heavy vehicle and trailer                                 •  Full inspection and measuring equipment

 •  DVSA/manufacturer information                            •  PPE, defect report and job-card evidence
